standard_prerequisites.name: The same statement for finite morphisms, established earlier in the same chapter (and by a previous card of this lane)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the conclusion in the finite case, to which the proof reduces.

standard_prerequisites.name: The affine structure theorem for quasi-finite morphisms, factoring the morphism as an open immersion followed by a finite morphism, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the affine intermediate scheme Z over which the morphism is finite.

standard_prerequisites.name: Nowhere density is local on the target, a finite union of closed nowhere dense subsets is nowhere dense, and the closure of the image of a closed nowhere dense subset under an open immersion is nowhere dense
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the reduction to an affine base, the reduction to one member of the affine cover, and the passage from the subset to its closure in the intermediate scheme.

core_obligations: Reduce to an affine base: as in the finite case the statement is local on the target, so one may assume the base affine, which makes the source a finite union of affine opens because the morphism is quasi-finite hence quasi-compact (proof lines 15260-15265).

Reduce to one chart: the traces of the closed nowhere dense subset on the members of the cover are nowhere dense, and a finite union of nowhere dense sets is nowhere dense, so it suffices to treat one affine chart of the source (proof lines 15266-15270).

Factor through a finite morphism: applying the affine structure theorem for quasi-finite morphisms gives an affine scheme through which the morphism factors as an open immersion followed by a finite morphism (proof lines 15270-15274).

Conclude: the closure of the image of the subset in the intermediate affine scheme is nowhere dense because the immersion is open, the image of the subset in the base is contained in the image of that closure under the finite morphism, and the finite case gives the conclusion (proof lines 15275-15284).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an affine base and to one affine chart of the source (proof lines 15260-15270).

Factor the chart morphism through a finite morphism via the affine structure theorem, transport the subset to its closure in the intermediate scheme, and invoke the finite case (proof lines 15270-15284).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that the image of a closed nowhere dense subset under a quasi-finite morphism is nowhere dense in the target (statement lines 15253-15258). The counted proof is a clean reduction carrying the content of the quasi-finite structure theorem: it reduces to an affine base and then to a single affine chart of the source, applies the factorization of a quasi-finite morphism as an open immersion followed by a finite morphism, observes that the closure of the image of the subset in the intermediate affine scheme is nowhere dense because the immersion is open, and concludes by the already established finite case (proof lines 15260-15284). It is H2: every reduction is carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the structure theorem and standard facts about nowhere dense sets.
